questions.prompt: It's turn one and your hand offers two openings. You...

answers.text: Put a unit on a battlefield and start scoring straight away.
Play a card that grows your runes for the rest of the game, and let them have the early lead.

questions.prompt: Two cheap spells, same cost. Which one makes your deck?

answers.text: Deals damage straight to an enemy unit.
Stuns an enemy unit so it sits out the next fight.

questions.prompt: Filling out your deck, you give more slots to...

answers.text: Units, and cards that make your units stronger.
Spells that answer whatever your opponent puts down.

questions.prompt: One spell slot left. It goes to a spell that...

answers.text: Creates two small soldier units.
Returns the best card in your trash to your hand.

questions.prompt: Your deck is one card over. Which do you cut?

answers.text: The card that wins the game by itself when it lands, and does nothing when it doesn't.
The card that's always useful and never spectacular.

questions.prompt: Two cards, same cost. You'd rather run the one that...

answers.text: Draws you two cards.
Gives you an extra rune for the rest of the game.

questions.prompt: Two decks are on the table. You'd rather pick up...

answers.text: The one with a single engine you lean on every turn. You'll be playing it sharply within a few games and can spend your attention on your opponent.
The one with several small pieces that combine differently every game. You'll still be finding new lines after twenty games.

questions.prompt: Which win feels better?

answers.text: Winning on turn nine with everything on the table.
Winning on turn four before they can react.

questions.prompt: You've just taken a battlefield. Next turn you'd rather...

answers.text: Dig in and hold it, with a trick ready for whoever comes to take it back.
Leave it and hit the next battlefield while they're off balance.

questions.prompt: A powerful effect asks a price. You'd rather pay by...

answers.text: Discarding a card from your hand.
Giving up one of your own units.

questions.prompt: You're about to attack and you have the numbers. You...

answers.text: Commit everything. If it lands, the game is as good as over.
Commit enough to force a response and keep the rest in reserve.

questions.prompt: It's your turn and you could spend every rune or keep some back. You...

answers.text: Keep some back so you can react to whatever they do on their turn.
Spend everything now and put another threat on the board.

questions.prompt: The most expensive card in your deck should be...

answers.text: A huge unit that wins any fight it's in.
A piece of gear that quietly takes over the game once it's in play.

questions.prompt: You have four cards to play this turn and the order matters. You...

answers.text: Enjoy it. Working out the exact order is the best bit.
Would rather play cards strong enough that the order takes care of itself.

questions.prompt: Which loss stings more?

answers.text: You were two turns from your plan coming together.
You had them on the ropes early, then they stabilised and ground you out.

questions.prompt: Two units, same cost and size. You'd rather run the one that...

answers.text: Takes the hits for the units beside it.
Hits harder whenever it's the one attacking.

questions.prompt: Add one unit to the deck:

answers.text: One that arrives with a small token unit: two bodies for one card.
One you can play face down and flip at the moment of your choosing.

questions.prompt: A deck that's unbeatable on its best days and falls apart on its worst is more fun than one that plays out the same way every game.
You need to cut a card. It's between...

answers.text: Your biggest unit.
Your best card-draw spell.

questions.prompt: The best moment in a game is when my opponent commits to a play and I have the exact answer waiting.
I want a game decided in the first few turns, whichever way it goes.
A huge enemy unit is parked on the battlefield you need. You'd rather...

answers.text: Attack into it with several units and finish it off with damage.
Stun it, or move it out of the way, and take the battlefield while it stands there.

questions.prompt: Your deck at its best feels like...

answers.text: A bag of tricks: cards changing places and surprises coming back from the trash.
A formation: every unit has a role and every loss pays for something.

questions.prompt: I play best with a deck that has one clear job, so I can focus on doing it well.
Your favourite kind of edge over an opponent is...

answers.text: More on the board: the bigger unit, the buff at the right moment.
More in hand: extra cards, and a face-down card they have to respect.

questions.prompt: Your deck wins with...

answers.text: Many threats spread across the deck, so losing any one barely matters.
One finisher the whole deck is built around. Drawing it is the game.
